protocol_metadata.name: IMCI Young Infant Protocol
protocol_metadata.source: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet, Management of the Sick Young Infant Aged Up to 2 Months, 2019

assess_young_infant.description: Initial visit. Assess the young infant in this exact order.
assess_young_infant.note: All classifications from all checks must be collected. Multiple classifications can co-exist. Treatment follows all applicable classifications.

check_psbi.title: Check for Possible Serious Bacterial Infection, Very Severe Disease, Pneumonia, or Local Bacterial Infection

urgent_pre_referral: Give first dose of intramuscular antibiotics (gentamicin + ampicillin).
Treat to prevent low blood sugar.
Advise the mother how to keep the infant warm on the way to hospital.
Give first dose of intramuscular antibiotics (gentamicin + ampicillin).
Treat to prevent low blood sugar.
Advise the mother how to keep the infant warm on the way to hospital.

treatment: Give oral amoxicillin for 7 days.
Advise the mother to give home care.
Follow up in 3 days.
Give amoxicillin for 5 days.
Teach the mother how to treat local infections at home.
Advise the mother to give home care.
Follow up in 2 days.

advice: Advise the mother on giving home care to the young infant.

check_psbi.resolution_rule: Select highest-priority classification whose criteria_any_of is satisfied. Only one PSBI-family classification is reported, but it can co-exist with classifications from other check nodes (jaundice, diarrhoea, etc.).

check_jaundice.source: IMCI Chart Booklet 2019, p.6 and p.26
check_jaundice.title: Check for Jaundice

treatment: Refer URGENTLY to hospital.
Advise the mother about home care.
Ask her to return for follow-up the next day.
Reassure the mother, continue home care.
Return for follow-up when the infant is 3 weeks of age.

follow_up.if_jaundice_beyond_3_weeks: Refer to hospital for further assessment.

check_diarrhoea.source: IMCI Chart Booklet 2019, p.7 and p.15-16
check_diarrhoea.title: Check for Diarrhoea and Dehydration
check_diarrhoea.gate_question: Does the young infant have diarrhoea? (Stools changed from usual pattern, frequent and watery)

if_no_other_severe_classification: Give fluid for severe dehydration (Plan C).
if_other_severe_classification_present: Give frequent sips of ORS on the way.
Advise the mother to continue breastfeeding.
Advise the mother how to keep the infant warm on the way.

treatment: Give fluid and breastmilk for some dehydration (Plan B).
if_other_severe_classification_present: Refer URGENTLY to hospital with frequent sips of ORS on the way.
Advise the mother to continue breastfeeding.

treatment: Give fluids and breastmilk at home (Plan A).

plan_c.title: Plan C: Treat Severe Dehydration Quickly

decision_path.question: Can you give intravenous fluid immediately?

actions: If the young infant can drink, give ORS by mouth while the drip is being set up.
Give 100 mL/kg body weight of Ringer's lactate solution (or normal saline if not available).
For infants <12 months: first give 30 mL/kg in 1 hour, then 70 mL/kg in 5 hours.
Reassess the young infant every 1-2 hours. If hydration not improving, give the intravenous drip more rapidly.
Also give ORS (about 5 mL/kg body weight per hour) as soon as the young infant can drink, usually after 3-4 hours.

no.next_question: Is intravenous treatment available nearby (within 30 minutes)?

actions: If the infant can drink, give the mother ORS solution and show her how to give frequent sips during the trip.
Or give ORS by nasogastric tube.

no.next_question: Are you trained to use a nasogastric tube for rehydration?

actions: Start rehydration by tube (or mouth) with ORS solution: give 20 mL/kg body weight per hour for 6 hours (total 120 mL/kg body weight).
Reassess the young infant every 1-2 hours while waiting for transfer.
If the infant vomits repeatedly or has abdominal distension, give the fluid more slowly.
If hydration is not improving after 3 hours, send the young infant for intravenous therapy.
After 6 hours, reassess the young infant. Classify dehydration. Then choose the appropriate plan (A, B, or C) to continue treatment.
Start rehydration by mouth with ORS solution: give 20 mL/kg body weight per hour for 6 hours (total 120 mL/kg body weight).
Reassess the young infant every 1-2 hours while waiting for transfer.
If the infant vomits repeatedly or has abdominal distension, give the fluid more slowly.
If hydration is not improving after 3 hours, send the young infant for intravenous therapy.
Refer URGENTLY to hospital for intravenous or nasogastric treatment.

plan_c.note: If the young infant is not referred to hospital, observe for at least 6 hours after rehydration to be sure the mother can maintain hydration giving ORS by mouth.

psbi_referral_refused.title: If Referral Is Refused or Not Feasible: Further Classify
psbi_referral_refused.when_to_use: Infant was classified with POSSIBLE_SERIOUS_BACTERIAL_INFECTION or VERY_SEVERE_DISEASE, but referral is refused or not feasible.

treatment: Reinforce URGENT referral. Explain to the caregiver that the infant is very sick and must be urgently referred.
If referral is still not feasible: give once-daily intramuscular gentamicin and twice-daily intramuscular ampicillin until referral is feasible or for 7 days.
Treat to prevent low blood sugar.
Teach the mother how to keep the young infant warm at home.
Advise the mother to return daily for injections.
Treat any other classification of illness in the young infant.
Reassess the young infant at each visit.
Give once-daily intramuscular gentamicin and oral amoxicillin for 7 days.
Treat to prevent low blood sugar.
Teach the mother how to keep the young infant warm at home.
Advise the mother to return for the next injection the following day.
Treat any other classification of illness in the young infant.
Reassess the young infant at each visit.
Give oral amoxicillin for 7 days.
Teach the mother how to give oral amoxicillin twice daily.
Treat any other classification of illness in the young infant.
Advise the mother to return for follow-up in 3 days.

psbi_referral_refused.resolution_rule: Select highest-priority classification whose criteria_any_of is satisfied.
